d3dx9.lib — Microsoft D3DX9 static library, as linked into lotrbfme.exe
=======================================================================

d3dx9.lib
  sha256  9496d4ce606998c2ad7588f2db9aada3c59786515244482230fde0cd6099ed56
  size    5,534,754 bytes
  dated   2003-09-09
  from    DirectX 9.0 SDK Update (Summer 2003), Lib/d3dx9.lib

Why this exact SDK
------------------
The retail exe embeds the string

    Microsoft (R) D3DX9 Shader Assembler 4.09.00.1126

which is the assembler version stamped into this release and no other. The
three neighbouring releases were checked and each one is a different build:
the 9.0/9.0a/9.0b lib (Dec 2002) carries no assembler stamp and reproduces
44.9% of the region, Summer 2004 stamps 5.04.00.2904 and reproduces 4.9%, and
December 2004 stamps 9.04.91.0000 and reproduces 2.8%. This lib reproduces
94.7% of it.

The game statically linked this library, so ~880 KB of the retail .text is
Microsoft's compiled code rather than the game's. Ledger rows sourced here
carry `vendored=d3dx9-summer2003` and name the archive member their bytes come
from; ./build.sh extracts that member and byte-compares it against retail like
any other row.

Region
------
RVA 0x009F9B82-0x00AD5401 (899,199 bytes, of which 885,799 are attached).
The lower bound is NOT 0x00A00000 — this file said 0x00A00000 while only one
d3dxmath.obj body had ever been attached, so the region below it read as
unowned. The run from 0x009F9B82 up to d3dx9's first attached row is
d3dxmath.obj laid out in object order — ?WithinEpsilon, ?sincosf,
c_D3DXFloat32To16Array, then the init_/c_ pairs in source sequence. dxerr9's
first attached row at 0x00AD5401 is the upper bound.

The run is d3dx9's, not d3dx9's exclusively. 0x00A62000-0x00A67000 interleaves
d3dx9's jpeg and png members with the game's own compiled
Code/Libraries/Source/{JPEG,LibPNG}/*.c — 58 game-source rows against 59 d3dx9
rows in that 20 KB. `in-window` is a fence between ARCHIVES, and a weaker one
than "everything here came from this lib".

How a row's ADDRESS is decided
------------------------------
Byte-matching a library body is easy and proves less than it looks. Every
relocation site in an archive member still holds an addend, so `./build.sh`
compares a lib row with those sites masked out — and a masked 40-byte span
with a conventional prologue can sit at several addresses. Picking one because
it matched is how a wave lands seventeen wrong addresses.

`tools/lib_window_sweep.py` decides an address under the COUNT-AGREEMENT
standard, which is three conditions, all required:

  in-window        the address is inside the run this archive owns. The four
                   libraries own four contiguous, non-overlapping runs of
                   [0x9F6C00, 0xB00000), so a d3dx9 body found inside dxerr9's
                   run is a coincidence, not a placement.
  count-agreement  retail holds no MORE copies of a body than the archive
                   supplies. Four in-window hits against three archive
                   instances means at least one hit is a collision and nothing
                   says which, so the whole equivalence class is refused.
  archive-order    with the counts agreeing, the i-th placement by ascending
                   RVA is the i-th instance in archive order.

Only archive-order can be wrong while every byte still matches, so four tests
exist to refute it, and each one refuses the whole class rather than repairing
a pair:

  ledger anchors   a class holding a body the ledger already attaches has a
                   known answer. 5 classes disagreed with it and went.
  callee targets   every REL32 in a claimed body is decoded out of retail and
                   the archive's own copy of the named callee must be at the
                   far end. `??_GCSprite` and `??_GCCodec` are 28 identical
                   bytes, but the one at 0x00A35FB5 calls 0x00A303D9 and only
                   ??1CCodec's body is there. 53 placements refused.
  DIR32 bases      a DIR32 slot says where a named global went, and a symbol
                   has one address: retail's dword minus the archive's addend
                   is that address. A placement putting an anchored symbol
                   somewhere an already-attached row does not is refused (7
                   placements: the ??_GCVSProgram/??_GCFXLProgram/??_GCPSProgram
                   three-way rotation, the ?SetAlloc@CArgument/@CInstruction
                   swap, two ??2CNode instantiations), and so is a pair of the
                   wave's own rows resolving one symbol two ways with nothing
                   attached to arbitrate (2 placements: _IID_ID3DXBuffer at
                   0x0114DA98 through one QueryInterface and 0x0114DBC8 through
                   the other).
  ghidra names     Ghidra has never seen this archive, so a name it recovers
                   from its own signatures is independent. Where it names one
                   candidate exactly, the class is settled: __RTC_Initialize at
                   0x009F7F0A is the one row in this wave that decides.

What is left when refutation runs out
-------------------------------------
The tests above say which assignments are WRONG. They do not make the survivor
unique. For each address the sweep now records every instance of the class that
survives all four, and 281 of the wave's 532 rows have more than one SYMBOL in
that set — 532-byte ?MatchIFCOND and ?MatchBREAK_COND are byte-identical in one
member and every REL32 in them goes to the same callee; 680-byte
?sse_D3DXMatrixInverse and ?sse2_D3DXMatrixInverse have no relocations at all.
Ascending order picks one. Nothing seconds it.

Those rows carry NO mangled name. They are named `?<lib>_twin_<rva>@@YAXXZ`,
with `object-symbol=` naming the COMDAT whose bytes they are and `lib-twin=<n>`
saying how many bodies could equally be here. The byte claim is untouched — the
gate resolves a lib row through `object-symbol=`, never through the name column
— and the headline does not move, because these bytes were already attached.
What stops is the name column asserting an identity the image does not witness:
that column is what every other tool resolves a symbol through, and a wave that
put real names on unwitnessed addresses is how 17 symbols ended up at wrong
RVAs one phase earlier.

The 251 rows that DO carry a real mangled name are the ones where exactly one
symbol survives. 5 of those still carry `<symbol>$<member>` because two members
define the one symbol; that name is a member disambiguator, not an identity
claim, and the function it names is the same either way.

Corroborations, and what each one cannot do
-------------------------------------------
- Relocation plausibility. Over the placements this standard produced, every
  relocation slot was read out of RETAIL and decoded: 0 of 742 REL32
  displacements point outside .text, 0 of 422 DIR32 words point outside the
  image. This rules out a needle landing at a random offset. It has ZERO power
  inside an equivalence class: the twins share their relocation offsets and the
  values are read out of the image, so a swapped assignment scores identically.
- Independent boundaries. Ghidra starts a function at 341 of the 532 addresses
  and agrees with the archive on the exact body length at all 341. This
  confirms the extent, not which twin.
- Independent names. Ghidra names three of them from its own signatures:
  __onexit at 0x009F6E00, __RTC_Initialize at 0x009F7F0A and
  _com_handle_excepinfo at 0x00AFE280, all three exactly where order-assignment
  put them and at the size the archive gives.
- Outgoing calls. 259 placements were confirmed by decoding a REL32 out of
  retail and finding the archive's own copy of the named callee at the far end.
  Read this as "the class is placed where its calls say it is", not as identity:
  where twins call the same function, a corroborated call corroborates the swap
  just as well, and those rows are in the 281 for exactly that reason.

The limitation, stated plainly
------------------------------
This standard is deliberately WEAKER than global uniqueness. It does not
establish that a body occurs at exactly one address in the image; it
establishes that the addresses it claims are inside the right library's run,
are not more numerous than the archive can account for, and are not contradicted
by a call, a global, an attached row or an independent name. Where several
identical bodies survive all of that, the row says so in its name.

The gate that says all this out loud
------------------------------------
`build.py`'s `verify_dir32_consistency` runs the DIR32 arithmetic over the
WHOLE ledger and fails on any symbol at two bases. It runs in the FULL gate
only: a ledger-only commit gets a scoped build from both the commit and the
push hook, and `main(only=...)` skips it. That is how this wave was pushed with
17 rows the check blames, and how master stayed red until they were retracted —
run `./build.sh` with no arguments before pushing a library wave, every time.

Two of those 17 buckets are worth keeping straight:
  - 7 rows were WRONG placements the check proved wrong. They are tombstoned
    with the attached row that witnesses the base and with the assignment the
    bases actually measure.
  - 10 rows (the sse_/sse2_ pairs) reference d3dxmathsse/d3dxmathsse2 constants
    that are IMAGE_SYM_CLASS_STATIC in BOTH objects: one name, two objects, two
    legitimate addresses. Those placements are byte-verified and uncontested;
    they come out because the check compares bases by symbol name. The fix is a
    storage-class exclusion in that check, not a whitelist entry — an 18-symbol
    whitelist block was added while master was red and has been removed, since
    it silenced the 7 real failures along with the 10 false ones.
`tools/lib_window_sweep.py` refuses, up front, both what its own DIR32 test
blames and what the gate's name-keyed rule will blame, so a wave cannot land in
that state again.

Re-deriving any of this
-----------------------
    python3 tools/lib_window_sweep.py --ledger-ref 9bbd26e53^ --detail out.csv

reads functions.csv from a git ref instead of the worktree, so a wave that has
already landed can be re-derived; the `candidates` column is the survivor set
each row's name is answerable to. Against today's rows every class this wave
claimed is already `consumed` and the sweep correctly reports nothing.

Re-obtaining the library
------------------------
    https://archive.org/download/dx90updatesdk/dx90updatesdk.exe   (191 MB)

A WEXTRACT self-extractor wrapping a CAB wrapping the inner installer; `7z x`
handles every layer. Extract to a real filesystem, not a tmpfs scratch dir.

Licence
-------
Redistribution of the DirectX SDK libraries is governed by the DirectX SDK
EULA. The file is committed as a build input for byte-verification only: it is
read to prove that retail bytes match Microsoft's shipped code, and none of it
is compiled into or redistributed as part of any binary this repo produces.
